title: 7 Things Scientists Just Learned About Whales
dek: From regional dialects to menopause and tool use, cetacean culture is vastly more complex than previously assumed.
author: Maya Sørensen
points: Sperm whales use rhythmic click accents that identify their specific clan.
Humpback song themes travel east across the Pacific in cultural waves.
Orca matriarchs lead hunting pods for decades after reproductive age.
Bowhead whales can live past 200 years with intact DNA repair mechanisms.

title: Why Deserts Aren't Really Empty
dek: Biological soil crusts—living matrices of cyanobacteria and lichens—hold the desert floor together like living glue.
author: Dr. Elena Vance
points: Cryptobiotic crusts can survive decades of total desiccation.
They fix atmospheric nitrogen and prevent devastating dust storms.
A single footprint can destroy a century of microbial growth.

title: The Strange Sound of the Deep Ocean
dek: In the SOFAR channel, acoustic energy is trapped and travels halfway around the globe without losing power.
author: Maya Sørensen
points: The Sound Fixing and Ranging channel acts as a natural deep-sea waveguide.
Fin whale calls in the Indian Ocean have been detected off Bermuda.
Undersea volcanic seismic rumbles provide real-time tectonic early warnings.

title: What Happens Inside a Volcano's Plumbing?
dek: Muon tomography uses cosmic ray particles to scan magma chambers like a medical X-ray.
author: Dr. Elena Vance
points: Cosmic ray muons penetrate hundreds of meters of solid basalt.
Detectors map magma column density shifts before physical swelling begins.
Helps predict explosive versus effusive eruption transitions.

title: How Trees Talk Through the Mycorrhizal Web
dek: Fungal hyphae interconnect tree root systems into a shared carbon and warning network.
author: Sarah Lin
points: Older 'hub trees' transfer carbon to shaded saplings through fungal filaments.
Pest attack warning chemicals trigger defensive tannin production in neighbors.
Soil disturbances fracture these vital ecological internet connections.

title: The Geometry of Pre-Solar Grains
dek: Tiny silicon carbide crystals found inside chondrite meteorites were formed in stars older than our Sun.
author: Dr. Arjun Patel
points: Diamond and graphite grains condensed in supernova ejecta 7 billion years ago.
Isotopic ratios preserve chemical snapshots of dead asymptotic giant stars.
We hold literal stardust in laboratory transmission electron microscopes.

title: Baking with 4,000-Year-Old Sourdough Yeast
dek: Microbiologists extract dormant yeast spores from ancient Egyptian ceramic beer vessels.
author: Tariq Al-Mansoor
points: Ancient ceramic pores protect dormant microbial endospores from degradation.
Culturing ancient Saccharomyces strains produces distinct aroma profiles.
Connects modern culinary science with Bronze Age fermentation practices.

title: Why Polar Snow is Never Truly White
dek: Cryophilic algae, black carbon, and mineral dust create a kaleidoscope of thermodynamic feedbacks.
author: Dr. Elena Vance
points: Watermelon snow is caused by Chlamydomonas nivalis synthesizing red carotenoids.
Darker snow absorbs more solar radiation, accelerating localized melting.
Glacier surfaces function as active microbial biological reactors.
